title: Collector permissions and audit schema conformance guide
content:
Purpose:
This working guide defines the operational contract between the evidence collectors, RBAC v2, and the centralized audit/SIEM pipeline. It focuses on two practical goals: (1) ensure collectors produce audit events that conform to the canonical audit schema and SIEM export mapping, and (2) define the minimum permission model (collector-facing subset of RBAC v2) and expected enforcement points. This doc is meant for collector implementers, SREs operating evidence pipelines, and security reviewers.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to: all active evidence collectors (edge agents, ingestion sidecars, and cloud-forwarders) that push control evidence into the central ingest pipeline.
- Not in scope: ad-hoc developer logging, debug traces, or internal application telemetry not flagged as "control evidence".

High-level decisions captured here:
- Wire format: JSONL (newline-delimited JSON) with UTF-8 encoding for ingress to the evidence gateway.
- Event signing: HMAC-SHA256 header signed by a collector-specific key derived from short-lived identity (see auth section).
- Minimum event fields: timestamp, event_id, event_type, actor, action, resource, outcome, evidence_id, artifact_hash, collector_id, sequence (monotonic per collector), schema_version.

RBAC v2: collector-facing permission model (summary)
We propose a compact permission set that maps cleanly to RBAC v2 roles in our directory service. Collector agents should operate under a principal that has exactly the permissions required to perform their functions. Enforcement points are: control-plane registration API, upload endpoints, and decommission/rotate key operations.

Permission names (collector-subset):
- collector:register  -> register a new collector and receive credentials
- collector:push-evidence -> push evidence batches to ingest endpoint
- collector:heartbeat -> send liveness probes (rate-limited)
- collector:read-config -> fetch collector config (sampling, redact rules)
- collector:rotate-keys -> request key rotation for credentials
- collector:decomission -> mark collector as decommissioned

Role examples (map to RBAC v2 roles):
- collector-runner (least privilege): collector:push-evidence, collector:heartbeat, collector:read-config
- collector-operator (operator persona): collector:register, collector:rotate-keys, collector:decommission, collector:read-config
- collector-admin (management): all collector-subset permissions + audit:read

Enforcement notes:
- The register endpoint verifies operator principal is in the collector-operator role.
- Tokens issued for collector-runner are scoped to a single collector_id and TTLed (~4 hours).
- All management operations are logged as control evidence events themselves (see sample audit events).

Audit event schema (conformance contract)
This is the minimum canonical schema collectors must emit. Additional vendor-specific fields are permitted under "metadata" but must not override canonical fields. Consumers downstream rely on canonical fields for rule detection and SIEM export.
- timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC string)
- event_id (UUIDv4)
- schema_version (string, e.g. "audit.v2")
- collector_id (string)
- actor { type, id }  -- flattened as actor_type and actor_id (see examples)
- action (string) -- short verb (install, start, push, rotate-key, delete)
- resource_type (string) -- e.g., "evidence-bundle", "collector-config"
- resource_id (string)
- outcome (string) -- success | failure | partial
- evidence_id (string) -- if action produces an evidence artifact
- artifact_hash (sha256 hex) -- when appropriate
- sequence (integer) -- monotonic increment per collector for ordering
- signature (base64) -- HMAC-SHA256 of the serialized body (header carries signature metadata)
- metadata (object) -- freeform key-values (note: allowed but not relied on for detection)

Example event (as one JSON line, remove whitespace when sending):
{
  "timestamp":"2026-02-12T19:25:34Z",
  "event_id":"b3f0d6d6-3c4b-4b2a-8e3a-2f6c9f4e1b55",
  "schema_version":"audit.v2",
  "collector_id":"col-aws-eu-17",
  "actor_type":"service_account",
  "actor_id":"svc-collector-123",
  "action":"push",
  "resource_type":"evidence-bundle",
  "resource_id":"evidence-20260212-000711",
  "outcome":"success",
  "evidence_id":"evi-9a2f3",
  "artifact_hash":"9f0c...ab3f",
  "sequence":1023,
  "signature":"BASE64SIG==",
  "metadata": { "origin_region":"eu-west-1","sampling":"full" }
}

Note: In the actual push the metadata object is allowed but the ingest parser will ignore unknown top-level fields. Make sure canonical names are preserved.

SIEM export mapping (consumer contract)
The central pipeline will export normalized fields to downstream SIEMs (Splunk, Sumo Logic, SIEM-X). Export rules: map canonical fields to SIEM-friendly names and enrich with lookup tables (teams, customer, environment). Maintain a stable mapping versioned alongside schema_version.
Example mapping (audit.v2 -> Splunk/Event):
- timestamp -> _time
- event_id -> event_id
- schema_version -> schema_version
- collector_id -> collector_id
- actor_type, actor_id -> user.type, user.id
- action -> verb
- resource_type, resource_id -> object.type, object.id
- outcome -> outcome
- evidence_id -> evidence_id
- artifact_hash -> artifact_hash

Transport and batching expectations
- Accept both single-line JSON and JSONL batches. The ingest gateway supports gzip compressed payloads; collectors SHOULD gzip batches > 64KB.
- Max uncompressed batch size: 10MB. Recommended per-batch item count: 1-500.
- The gateway provides per-collector backpressure via HTTP 429 with Retry-After and a per-collector pending-queue-length metric.

Auth and signing model (summary)
- Registration flow uses operator credentials (RBAC-scoped) to call POST /v1/collectors/register and returns short-lived X.509 cert + collector_id.
- Collector uses mTLS (preferred) or Bearer token (secondary) to call /v1/collectors/push.
- Each push request must include a signature header X-Collector-Signature:sha256=<base64> of the body and the collector_id in X-Collector-Id header. The gateway verifies TTL, signature, and that the principal still has collector:push-evidence permission.

Collector plugin interface (developer notes)
- Minimal endpoints to implement on a plugin shim:
  - register(operator_token) -> returns {collector_id, cert, enroll_key_ttl}
  - push(batch_jsonl, signature, collector_id) -> 202 | 4xx
  - heartbeat(collector_id, seq) -> 200 | 401
  - fetch-config(collector_id) -> json (sampling, redaction rules)

Operational runbook (quick start)
- On 401 or signature failures: rotate collector key, verify register call logs, confirm RBAC membership for operator account.
- On repeated 429s: check gateway queue length, reduce batch size, enable compression.
- Missing sequence numbers: run replay job using sequence+range pull from collector local store (collector must keep last 10K events).
- Evidence corruption (hash mismatch): quarantined, alert security with correlation id, run artifact re-ingest if available.

Rollout and e2e test checklist
- Unit tests: validate canonical fields present and types.
- Contract tests: push golden JSONL to staging gateway and verify parser acceptance and SIEM mapping outputs.
- RBAC test: attempt management ops with a collector-runner token (expect deny), exercise rotate with collector-operator (expect success).
- Chaos test: simulate 50% packet loss between collector and gateway, ensure backoff and no silent data loss.

Migration notes for legacy collectors
- Legacy collectors that emit "audit.v1" should be routed through a translation adapter for 6 months. During that window, incidents flagged by detection rules must log both original and translated event ids to support incident correlation.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide canonical retention period tag placement (should retention metadata live in metadata.retention_days or top-level retention_days?).
- Approve HSM key lifecycle for collector registration tokens (security review assigned to Priya Nair).
- Add formal schema registry entry and automated schema validation in the ingest pipeline (JIRA-SCHEMA-89).

Notes / references
- See linked Confluence page for historical notes and prior prototypes.
- This doc will be picked into the evidence automation guild backlog for implementation scheduling.

Owner and contacts:
- Primary owner: Hannah Liu (security-and-compliance)
- Implementation leads: Marcus Reed (ingest), Priya Nair (collector SDK), Diego Alvarez (SRE)

Appendix: quick validation script (pseudocode)
- Validate presence/type of canonical fields
- Verify signature computed over canonical field ordering
- Check sequence monotonicity per collector id

End of guide.
